explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, double-peaked effect. Demand is at its lowest in the very early morning (around 4 a.m., contribution ≈ −3.2 in log space), climbs sharply from 5 a.m. onward, reaches a first peak at 8 a.m. (contribution ≈ +0.54), dips slightly in mid-morning, then surges to its highest point at 5 p.m. (contribution ≈ +0.80), before falling steadily back to near-zero by midnight.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the strongest feature in the model (rank 1, importance 0.83) — roughly four times more influential than the next feature. Getting the time-of-day pattern right is the single biggest driver of the model's predictions.

---
[RECOMMENDATION] Hour of the day and temperature are overwhelmingly the strongest demand drivers, so staffing and bike redistribution plans should first be built around the two daily rush-hour peaks (morning around 8 a.m. and evening around 5 p.m.) and then adjusted upward or downward based on the day's forecast temperature — scaling up resources for mild, warm days and scaling back for very cold or very hot conditions.
